author: Thomas à Kempis
title: That Holy Communion is not lightly to be omitted

verses.text: The Voice of the Beloved
verses.modernizedText: The Voice of the Beloved

verses.text: Thou must frequently betake thee to the Fountain of grace and divine mercy, to the Fountain of goodness and all purity; to the end that thou mayest obtain the healing of thy passions and vices, and mayest be made stronger and more watchful against all temptations and wiles of the devil.
verses.modernizedText: You must frequently turn to the Fountain of grace and divine mercy, to the Fountain of goodness and all purity, so that you may obtain the healing of your passions and vices, and may be made stronger and more watchful against all temptations and wiles of the devil.

verses.text: The enemy, knowing what profit and exceeding strong remedy lieth in the Holy Communion, striveth by all means and occasions to draw back and hinder the faithful and devout, so far as he can.
verses.modernizedText: The enemy, knowing what profit and exceedingly strong remedy lie in Holy Communion, strives by all means and occasions to draw back and hinder the faithful and devout, so far as he can.

verses.text: For when some set about to prepare themselves for Holy Communion, they suffer from the more evil suggestions of Satan.
verses.modernizedText: For when some set about preparing themselves for Holy Communion, they suffer from the more evil suggestions of Satan.

verses.text: The very evil spirit himself (as is written in Job), cometh among the sons of God that he may trouble them by his accustomed evil dealing, or make them over timid and perplexed; to the intent that he may diminish their affections, or take away their faith by his attacks, if haply he may prevail upon them to give up Holy Communion altogether, or to come thereto with lukewarm hearts.
verses.modernizedText: The very evil spirit himself (as is written in Job) comes among the sons of God that he may trouble them by his accustomed evil dealing, or make them overly timid and perplexed; with the intent that he may diminish their affections, or take away their faith by his attacks, if perhaps he may prevail upon them to give up Holy Communion altogether, or to come to it with lukewarm hearts.

verses.text: But his wiles and delusions must not be heeded, howsoever wicked and terrible they be; but all his delusion must be cast back upon his own head.
verses.modernizedText: But his wiles and delusions must not be heeded, however wicked and terrible they are; but all his delusion must be cast back upon his own head.

verses.text: The wretch must be despised and laughed to scorn: neither must Holy Communion be omitted because of his insults and the inward troubles which he stirreth up.
verses.modernizedText: The wretch must be despised and laughed to scorn; neither must Holy Communion be omitted because of his insults and the inward troubles which he stirs up.

verses.text: Often also too much carefulness or some anxiety or other touching confession hindereth from obtaining devotion.
verses.modernizedText: Often also too much carefulness or some anxiety or other concerning confession hinders one from obtaining devotion.

verses.text: Do thou according to the counsel of wise men, and lay aside anxiety and scruple, because it hindereth the grace of God and destroyeth devotion of mind.
verses.modernizedText: Do according to the counsel of wise men, and lay aside anxiety and scruple, because it hinders the grace of God and destroys devotion of mind.

verses.text: Because of some little vexation or trouble do not thou neglect Holy Communion, but rather hasten to confess it, and forgive freely all offences committed against thee.
verses.modernizedText: Because of some little vexation or trouble do not neglect Holy Communion, but rather hasten to confess it, and forgive freely all offenses committed against you.

verses.text: And if thou hast offended any man, humbly beg for pardon, and God shall freely forgive thee.
verses.modernizedText: And if you have offended any man, humbly beg for pardon, and God will freely forgive you.

verses.text: What profiteth it to put off for long time the confession of thy sins, or to defer Holy Communion?
verses.modernizedText: What good does it do to put off for a long time the confession of your sins, or to defer Holy Communion?

verses.text: Cleanse thyself forthwith, spit out the poison with all speed, hasten to take the remedy, and thou shalt feel thyself better than if thou didst long defer it.
verses.modernizedText: Cleanse yourself immediately, spit out the poison with all speed, hasten to take the remedy, and you will feel yourself better than if you long deferred it.

verses.text: If to-day thou defer it on one account, to-morrow perchance some greater obstacle will come, and so thou mayest be long time hindered from Communion and become more unfit.
verses.modernizedText: If today you defer it on one account, tomorrow perhaps some greater obstacle will come, and so you may be hindered from Communion a long time and become more unfit.

verses.text: As soon as thou canst, shake thyself from thy present heaviness and sloth, for it profiteth nothing to be long anxious, to go long on thy way with heaviness of heart, and because of daily little obstacles to sever thyself from divine things: nay it is exceeding hurtful to defer thy Communion long, for this commonly bringeth on great torpor.
verses.modernizedText: As soon as you can, shake yourself from your present heaviness and sloth, for it profits nothing to be anxious long, to go long on your way with heaviness of heart, and because of daily little obstacles to sever yourself from divine things: indeed it is exceedingly hurtful to defer your Communion long, for this commonly brings on great torpor.

verses.text: Alas! there are some, lukewarm and undisciplined, who willingly find excuses for delaying repentance, and desire to defer Holy Communion, lest they should be bound to keep stricter watch upon themselves.
verses.modernizedText: Alas! there are some, lukewarm and undisciplined, who willingly find excuses for delaying repentance, and desire to defer Holy Communion, lest they should be bound to keep stricter watch upon themselves.

verses.text: Alas! how little charity, what flagging devotion, have they who so lightly put off Holy Communion.
verses.modernizedText: Alas! how little charity, what flagging devotion, have those who so lightly put off Holy Communion.

verses.text: How happy is he, how acceptable to God, who so liveth, and in such purity of conscience keepeth himself, that any day he could be ready and well inclined to communicate, if it were in his power, and might be done without the notice of others.
verses.modernizedText: How happy is he, how acceptable to God, who so lives, and keeps himself in such purity of conscience, that any day he could be ready and well inclined to communicate, if it were in his power, and might be done without the notice of others.

verses.text: If a man sometimes abstaineth for the sake of humility or some sound cause, he is to be commended for his reverence.
verses.modernizedText: If a man sometimes abstains for the sake of humility or some sound cause, he is to be commended for his reverence.

verses.text: But if drowsiness have taken hold of him, he ought to rouse himself and to do what in him lieth; and the Lord will help his desire for the good will which he hath, which God specially approveth.
verses.modernizedText: But if drowsiness has taken hold of him, he ought to rouse himself and to do what lies in him; and the Lord will help his desire because of the good will which he has, which God specially approves.

verses.text: But when he is hindered by sufficient cause, yet will he ever have a good will and pious intention to communicate; and so he shall not be lacking in the fruit of the Sacrament.
verses.modernizedText: But when he is hindered by sufficient cause, yet he will ever have a good will and pious intention to communicate; and so he will not be lacking in the fruit of the Sacrament.

verses.text: For any devout man is able every day and every hour to draw near to spiritual communion with Christ to his soul’s health and without hindrance.
verses.modernizedText: For any devout man is able every day and every hour to draw near to spiritual communion with Christ for his soul’s health and without hindrance.

verses.text: Nevertheless on certain days and at the appointed time he ought to receive the Body and Blood of his Redeemer with affectionate reverence, and rather to seek after the praise and honour of God, than his own comfort.
verses.modernizedText: Nevertheless on certain days and at the appointed time he ought to receive the Body and Blood of his Redeemer with affectionate reverence, and rather to seek after the praise and honor of God than his own comfort.

verses.text: For so often doth he communicate mystically, and is invisibly refreshed, as he devoutly calleth to mind the mystery of Christ’s incarnation and His Passion, and is inflamed with the love of Him.
verses.modernizedText: For as often as he devoutly calls to mind the mystery of Christ’s incarnation and His Passion, and is inflamed with the love of Him, so often does he communicate mystically and is invisibly refreshed.

verses.text: He who only prepareth himself when a festival is at hand or custom compelleth, will too often be unprepared.
verses.modernizedText: He who only prepares himself when a festival is at hand or custom compels him will too often be unprepared.

verses.text: Blessed is he who offereth himself to God for a whole burnt-offering, so often as he celebrateth or communicateth!
verses.modernizedText: Blessed is he who offers himself to God for a whole burnt offering, as often as he celebrates or communicates!

verses.text: Be not too slow nor too hurried in thy celebrating, but preserve the good received custom of those with whom thou livest.
verses.modernizedText: Do not be too slow or too hurried in your celebrating, but preserve the good received custom of those with whom you live.

verses.text: Thou oughtest not to produce weariness and annoyance in others, but to observe the received custom, according to the institution of the elders; and to minister to the profit of others rather than to thine own devotion or feeling.
verses.modernizedText: You ought not to produce weariness and annoyance in others, but to observe the received custom, according to the institution of the elders; and to minister to the profit of others rather than to your own devotion or feeling.
